column4: Tesla says this car can hit sixty in under one second.
But what would that do to your body?
At launch, you'd feel almost three G's.
Your head snaps back. Your eleven pound head suddenly feels like thirty three pounds.
Your organs lag behind. Your stomach squishes back toward your spine.
Here's the surprise. You won't black out.
Fighter pilots black out when blood drains down, away from the brain.
But sitting back, your blood stays level with your head. Your brain keeps its oxygen.
Less than a second later, you're at sixty. You've gone about forty feet. One city bus.
The scary part isn't going. It's stopping. Anything loose keeps flying at sixty.
Would your neck survive? Subscribe for more.
